A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Cumulative Reasoning work and contain complete main text and Appendices A-F. Full text extraction and rendered-page comparisons support reliable comparison of their text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v9 reports original CR experiments on logical inference, Game of 24, and MATH, including accuracy comparisons, search costs, and component ablations.

after.justification: v10 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and the conceptual experiment in Table 1. These qualify independently of Appendix B's explicitly attributed third-party results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same Proposer, Verifier, and Reporter procedure, cumulative DAG construction, and task-specific adaptations. The code-verifier integration and Appendix F prompts are unchanged.

E1.justification: FOLIO-wiki, its curated subset, AutoTNLI, Game of 24, and MATH coverage is unchanged. Appendix B retains the same LogiQA, ProofWriter, FOLIO-val, and LD comparisons, and the appendix examples are retained.

E2.justification: The comparator sets remain unchanged within corresponding experiments, including Direct, CoT, CoT-SC, ToT, Complex CoT, PAL, and ToRA. Bibliographic updates do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both versions report the same models, prompting configurations, temperatures, metrics, and search settings. The 100-puzzle Game of 24 evaluation and 500-example MATH subset are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 1's two-stage reasoning experiment, Table 5's component ablations, Table 7's breadth comparisons, and the appendix reasoning examples and dataset error analyses are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Table 1 states in both versions that each case was repeated 1,000 times. Repetition information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged; no confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative outcomes are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. Examples include CR's 98.04% FOLIO-wiki-curated accuracy in Table 3, 98% Game of 24 accuracy in Table 7, and 72.2% MATH accuracy with code in Table 11.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Assumption 3.2, Lemma 3.3, Theorem 3.4, and the Appendix A proofs are unchanged. Surrounding punctuation edits and Appendix C's citation removal do not revise the mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims concerning cumulative verified reasoning and its advantages on logical inference, Game of 24, and MATH.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, Appendix B.2's computational tradeoffs, and Appendix C's FOL/HOL limitations are unchanged in substance. Removing the expressiveness citation does not change the associated limitation.

D1.justification: The Guidance implementation description, model and decoding details, Appendix E's curation information, Appendix F's prompt templates, and project access link are unchanged.

R1.justification: v10 removes the Löwenheim (1967) citation from Appendix C's expressiveness discussion and deletes its bibliography entry. Updates to Kumar, Ma, and Wang entries concern existing works' publication metadata; the broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v10 makes limited wording and punctuation edits, including correcting 'aims to operationalizes' to 'aims to operationalize,' and updates bibliographic metadata. It also introduces the visible title misspelling 'Large anguage Models.' Section order and the narrative remain stable.

P2.justification: The title and author-name typography changes, and the title occupies one line instead of two. This causes limited opening-page reflow and shifts Figure 1 vertically; references and Appendix C also reflow locally. Figures and tables retain their content and designs.

improvement.justification: The scientific content and evidence are unchanged. Although v10 offers small copyediting improvements and fuller publication details, it replaces v9's correctly spelled title with the prominent visible error 'Large anguage Models.' This new title error outweighs the limited editorial polish, leaving presentation slightly worse overall.
